title: QSPI and OSPI overview: select memory protocol and boot behavior
summary: Check controller, package and memory compatibility, transfer mode and command timing before choosing a serial-memory connection.
applies_to: External serial memory planning; STM32 examples are scoped to their listed devices.
required_inputs: Exact controller/memory, voltage, mode and boot requirements
verification: Check initialization, dummy cycles and memory-mapped operation against both devices.
limitations: QSPI and OSPI are not interchangeable capabilities; consult errata and exact device guides.

title: QSPI point-to-point flash routing pattern
summary: Connect the selected clock, chip select and data pins consistently; keep the memory channel compact and preserve its reference.
applies_to: Single QSPI memory; STM32F4 layout guidance is an example.
required_inputs: Pin mapping, timing budget and fabrication construction
verification: Check clock/data timing and reads across the intended operating conditions.
limitations: ST example dimensions are not universal limits for other controllers or packages.

placement: Place flash near its controller interface.
routing: Limit transitions; evaluate clock separation and data skew.
return_path: Keep an uninterrupted reference under the channel.
pitfalls: Do not copy an example length tolerance into another timing budget.

title: OSPI data-strobe and calibration review
summary: Determine whether the selected memory mode uses a data strobe and how the controller samples it. Include supported delay-block or PHY calibration in bring-up.
applies_to: Strobe-capable serial-memory controllers; ST AN5050 describes specific STM32 implementations.
required_inputs: Controller/memory mode, strobe timing and supported calibration procedure
verification: Review data/strobe timing and repeat transfer checks across intended operating conditions.
limitations: No universal DQS length tolerance or register value is supplied. HyperBus and regular-command protocols need separate configuration.
